3	description: GuideMate WSL render dilemma — GPU (d3d12) is fast but BREAKS sensors (lidar all range_min); software renders sensors correctly but slow. Must use software + strip sensors for speed.
4	metadata:
5	  node_type: memory

8	---
9	
10	**HEADLINE (2026-07-05): On this WSL box, GPU GL rendering BREAKS Gazebo sensors. Use SOFTWARE rendering (`LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1`) for anything that needs lidar/camera.** Do NOT re-try d3d12/zink for the sim — both were fully tested and rejected. `sim_start.sh` supports `RENDER=software|gpu|zink` (default gpu is FAST but SENSOR-BROKEN; use `RENDER=software`).
11	
12	The render backends, tested (world=maze):
13	- **d3d12 GPU** (RTX 3050 or AMD iGPU via WSLg): sim runs fast (RTF ~0.067, 4.6x) BUT **all 640 lidar beams read range_min (0.164) = garbage**. GPU renders the GUI fine but offscreen sensor depth readback is broken. Useless for SLAM/nav.
14	- **zink** (GL-on-Vulkan): Gazebo can't create a GL context at all — `glx: failed to create drisw screen`, OGRE `Unable to create glx context`, Qt aborts, gazebo process dies. Non-viable.
15	- **software (llvmpipe)**: valid lidar (ranges 1.0-11.6m, 639/640 valid) BUT slow (RTF ~0.015 with GUI + all sensors). THE ONLY MODE WITH WORKING SENSORS.
16	
17	Why: Gazebo renders sensors through OGRE's GLX path (`Sensors.cc → Loading plugin [gz-rendering-ogre]`), same context type as the GUI. The WSL GPU GL drivers mishandle offscreen render-to-texture depth.
18	
19	**Speed fix under software (SOLVED, RTF 0.02 → 0.634 = 32x):** two levers, applied together:
20	1. **Physics timestep** — `maze.sdf` (`irobot_create_gz_bringup/worlds/maze.sdf`) `max_step_size` 0.001→0.004, `real_time_update_rate` 1000→250. 4x less physics work; fine for a flat diffdrive robot. This was a big part of the win.
21	2. **Sensor render-rate flood** — the killer was ~11 create3 ray sensors (4 cliff + 7 IR) each rendering at **62 Hz** = ~680 render passes/sec on the CPU. Dropped to 2 Hz in `irobot_create_description/urdf/sensors/{cliff_sensor,ir_intensity,ir_opcode_receivers}.urdf.xacro` (the `update_rate` prop/param). NOTE: stripping the OAK-D camera barely helped (only 30 passes/sec) — the 62 Hz ray-sensor count was the real flood.
22	Also done earlier: camera sensor commented out in `turtlebot4_description/urdf/sensors/oakd.urdf.xacro`; rplidar 62→10 Hz in `rplidar.urdf.xacro`; headless (`sim_start_headless.sh` + `sim_headless.launch.py`, server-only `gz sim -s`) — headless alone barely helped in software (GUI wasn't the cost). All edited vendor files have `.stock.bak` backups (chown'd to user). **Whenever the sim is relaunched, sim time resets to 0 — RESTART slam_toolbox (and any use_sim_time node), else it freezes rejecting "past" timestamps.** Final viable config: `RENDER=software` + headless + physics 4ms/250 + create3 sensors 2 Hz → RTF ~0.63, valid lidar.
23	
24	Also fixed this session: `sim_start.sh` had `set -u` which crashed on ROS `setup.bash` (unbound AMENT_TRACE_SETUP_FILES) — wrapped in `set +u`/`set -u`. `mesa-utils` installed (glxinfo). Clock knob useless below RTF 1.0; robot-SPEED is the only useful runtime speed lever. See [[guidemate-sim-facts]], [[guidemate-mvp-plan]], [[debugging-step-back-over-detail-drilling]].
25

3	description: GuideMate laptop WSL networking — mirrored mode broke ROS2 DDS; switched to NAT (CONFIRMED FIXED)
4	metadata: 
5	  node_type: memory
6	  type: project

8	---
9	
10	STATUS 2026-07-04: FIXED & CONFIRMED. Switching WSL from mirrored to NAT solved the sim; step 1 is done.
11	
12	Problem: On Shibo's Lenovo laptop (AMD 6900HS + RTX 3050), the ROS2 Jazzy + Gazebo TB4 sim launched but inter-node DDS comm was broken/degraded — dark LEDs, controllers slow (125s) or failing, `ros2 topic list` daemon hanging, flaky topic delivery, hundreds of SHM `open_and_lock_file` errors.
13	
14	Root cause: WSL2 **mirrored** networking mode (`/mnt/c/Users/76405/.wslconfig` had `networkingMode=mirrored`, `firewall=true`). Mirrored makes ROS nodes share the Windows network stack, so DDS crosses the Hyper-V firewall + a messy interface set (loopback0, extra lo addr 10.255.255.254, /16 eth2). Decisive proof it was the network (not SHM/scripts): comm failed even with shared memory fully disabled. Ruled out: hardware (GPU idle under software rendering) and SHM (harmless UDP-fallback noise, maybe worsened by Lenovo OEM security). The Canada desktop had worked because it used NAT.
15	
16	Fix applied: `.wslconfig` → `[wsl2] networkingMode=NAT / dnsTunneling=true / autoProxy=false` (original saved to `.wslconfig.mirrored.bak`). Proxy in `~/.bashrc` changed from Clash@127.0.0.1:7890 (mirrored) to Windows-host-IP: `WIN_HOST=$(ip route show default | awk '{print $3}')` → `http(s)_proxy=http://$WIN_HOST:7890`, `all_proxy=socks5://$WIN_HOST:7891` — **requires Clash "Allow LAN" enabled**. #!/usr/bin/env python3
"""GuideMate SLAM driver: reactive left-hand wall-follower (lidar-only).

Drives the namespaced TB4 around a maze to build a slam_toolbox map, hands-off.
- Subscribes /robot_1/scan (SensorDataQoS = BEST_EFFORT, matches the gz lidar).
- Publishes geometry_msgs/Twist to /robot_1/cmd_vel_unstamped (no stamp check).
Left-hand rule: keep the wall on the LEFT at ~target distance; turn right when the
front is blocked; curve left to reacquire when the left opens up. Speeds kept modest
so SLAM scan-matching stays clean (fast rotation smears loop closure).
"""
import math
import rclpy
from rclpy.node import Node
from rclpy.qos import qos_profile_sensor_data
from sensor_msgs.msg import LaserScan
from geometry_msgs.msg import Twist

NS = '/robot_1'

# tunables
TARGET_LEFT = 0.6      # desired distance to left wall (m)
WALL_DETECT = 1.5      # left reading below this => a wall is present to follow
FRONT_STOP = 0.7       # if anything closer than this ahead, turn away
LIN_SPEED = 0.30       # forward speed (m/s); TB4 max ~0.31 (speed = key lever at low RTF)
TURN = 0.8             # base angular speed (rad/s)
HYST = 0.15            # deadband around TARGET_LEFT (m)
SECTOR = math.radians(25)  # half-width of each sampling sector


class WallFollower(Node):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__('wall_follower')
        self.pub = self.create_publisher(Twist, f'{NS}/cmd_vel_unstamped', 10)
        self.sub = self.create_subscription(
            LaserScan, f'{NS}/scan', self.on_scan, qos_profile_sensor_data)
        self.timer = self.create_timer(0.1, self.tick)   # 10 Hz control
        self.front = self.left = self.right = float('inf')
        self.have_scan = False
        self.n = 0
        self.get_logger().info('wall_follower up; waiting for scan...')

    def sector_min(self, msg, center):
        """Min valid range in a sector centered at angle `center` (rad)."""
        best = float('inf')
        for i, r in enumerate(msg.ranges):
            if not math.isfinite(r) or r <= msg.range_min:
                continue
            a = msg.angle_min + i * msg.angle_increment
            # wrap difference into [-pi, pi]
            d = math.atan2(math.sin(a - center), math.cos(a - center))
            if abs(d) <= SECTOR and r < best:
                best = r
        return best

    def on_scan(self, msg):
        self.front = self.sector_min(msg, 0.0)
        self.left = self.sector_min(msg, math.pi / 2)
        self.right = self.sector_min(msg, -math.pi / 2)
        self.have_scan = True

    def tick(self):
        if not self.have_scan:
            return
        t = Twist()
        if self.front < FRONT_STOP:
            # blocked ahead -> rotate right in place (away from left wall)
            t.linear.x = 0.0
            t.angular.z = -TURN
        elif self.left > WALL_DETECT:
            # NO left wall nearby (open space) -> drive forward to FIND one,
            # only a gentle left bias so we spiral out instead of circling in place.
            t.linear.x = LIN_SPEED
            t.angular.z = TURN * 0.25
        elif self.left > TARGET_LEFT + HYST:
            # wall present but drifting away -> curve left to close the gap
            t.linear.x = LIN_SPEED
            t.angular.z = TURN * 0.4
        elif self.left < TARGET_LEFT - HYST:
            # too close to left wall -> ease right
            t.linear.x = LIN_SPEED
            t.angular.z = -TURN * 0.4
        else:
            # good corridor, wall at target distance -> straight
            t.linear.x = LIN_SPEED
            t.angular.z = 0.0
        self.pub.publish(t)
        self.n += 1
        if self.n % 20 == 0:  # ~every 2s
            self.get_logger().info(
                f'front={self.front:.2f} left={self.left:.2f} right={self.right:.2f} '
                f'-> v={t.linear.x:.2f} w={t.angular.z:.2f}')


def main():
    rclpy.init()
    node = WallFollower()
    try:
        rclpy.spin(node)
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        pass
    finally:
        node.pub.publish(Twist())  # stop the robot on exit
        node.destroy_node()
        rclpy.shutdown()


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
